context.name: cybion_list_contexts
context.description: List top-level Contexts (context_id, name, description, source) from the controller: first the read-only Cybion Common Context (source "common"; product usage guidance compiled into the controller), then the user's own Contexts (source "local"). Content is intentionally omitted; use read_context to read a context and discover its direct children.

context.name: cybion_list_workers
context.description: List owned and shared Workers (worker_id, label, owner_user_id, access) from the controller. Every Worker tool call must include an exact worker_id from this list; never choose a Worker implicitly. Registered Workers are not necessarily online; availability is checked when a Worker tool is called.

context.name: read_context
context.description: Read the full content of a context and its direct children metadata (context_id, name, description) from the controller. Start from a context_id listed by cybion_list_contexts; pass a returned child context_id to explore further levels. Reads resolve local Contexts first, then the read-only Cybion Common Context.

context_id.description: Exact context_id from cybion_list_contexts or from children returned by a previous read_context call.

context.name: write_context
context.description: Edit one of the user's local Contexts from the controller — its title, its Use When description, its body, and its parent. Omit a field to keep its current value; parent_id takes an exact context_id, null to move the Context to the top level, or the special value "TRASH" to move it into the trash. A trashed Context disappears from every Context tool, while the user still sees it in the Contexts page and can restore it. Returns the updated Context metadata. The read-only Cybion Common Context cannot be written, and a Context hidden by the trash cannot be written until it is restored.

context_id.description: Exact context_id of the local Context to edit, from cybion_list_contexts or a child listed by read_context.

name.description: New title, 1-160 characters. Omit to keep the current title.

description.description: New Use When description — the condition for when this Context should be read (up to 10,000 characters). Omit to keep the current description.

content.description: New Markdown body (up to 200,000 characters). Omit to keep the current body.

parent_id.description: New parent: an exact context_id to become a child of that Context, null to move to the top level, or "TRASH" to move the Context into the trash where the user can still see and restore it. Omit to keep the current parent.

context.name: cybion_list_ultimate_machines
context.description: List the user's Ultimate Machines (终极机器): scheduled self-checks that run one bash command on a Worker every interval and stay silent while the command exits 0. A failing run is delivered into the machine's repair Thread (终极机器 · <name>) as a user message asking to make the command return 0 — dropped, not queued, while that Thread is mid-turn; an offline or missing Worker is reported once per episode through Linkit; a run that never settles is declared lost after 15 minutes and reported once. Returns id, name, worker_id, worker_label, command, intent, interval_seconds, enabled, last_run_at, last_exit, thread_id, created_at. Use it to pick a machine_id for cybion_get_ultimate_machine or cybion_set_ultimate_machine.

context.name: cybion_get_ultimate_machine
context.description: Read one Ultimate Machine by machine_id: its definition (name, worker_id, command, intent, interval_seconds, enabled), its bound repair Thread, and the latest settled run — last_run_at plus last_exit, where 0 is healthy, any other number is the Unix exit code (a command killed without one counts as -1), and null means the latest run produced no exit code (no run yet, a run lost mid-flight, or an execution error reported through Linkit). Use it to inspect a machine before editing it, or to relate a 【终极机器·<name>】 repair request to the machine that sent it.

context.name: cybion_set_ultimate_machine
context.description: Create or update an Ultimate Machine (终极机器) — one bash command run on one Worker every interval_seconds, silent while the command exits 0. Omit machine_id to create: name, worker_id, command and interval_seconds are required, the first run starts right away, and a repair Thread named 终极机器 · <name> is created automatically. Pass machine_id to update — only the fields you give change, and: an empty intent clears it; enabled pauses or resumes; a new worker_id starts a fresh offline-notification episode; renaming retitles the repair Thread unless the user renamed it by hand. Machines cannot be deleted here: pause with enabled=false, or delete the bound Thread or its Worker. To validate a check immediately, run the same command with bash on the Worker — the next scheduled run re-verifies silently.

machine_id.description: Omit to create a new machine; pass the exact id from cybion_list_ultimate_machines to update that machine.

name.description: Label shown in the Ultimate Machines list, 1-120 characters, e.g. 磁盘检查. On create required.

worker_id.description: Exact worker_id from cybion_list_workers, of a Worker you own — shared Workers cannot run machines. The command runs there through the normal Worker protocol (bash with timeout_seconds=300). On create required; changing it moves the machine and restarts the offline-notification episode.

command.description: The single bash command run every interval; 1-4000 characters. Exit 0 means healthy and silent; any other result is sent to the repair Thread with the tail of stderr/stdout (up to 1500 characters), so make failures self-explanatory. Keep it cheap and safe to repeat. On create required. Example: test $(df -Pk / | awk 'NR==2 {print $5}' | tr -d %) -lt 90

intent.description: Optional plain-language goal of the check, up to 2000 characters, e.g. 确保根分区低于 90%. Delivered with every repair request (意图) so the fixing agent knows what the check protects. On update, omit to keep it and pass an empty string to clear it.

interval_seconds.description: Seconds between runs, 10-2592000 (30 days). The first run starts right after creation; afterwards the next run starts one interval after the previous run settled, with at most one run in flight. On create required.

enabled.description: Update only: false pauses all runs and notices, true resumes. A new machine starts enabled.

worker.name: bash
worker.description: Run a shell command on the user's selected Worker. To wait before the command runs, set delay_seconds instead of embedding a `sleep`: embedded sleeps count toward Worker call duration and misreport Worker performance.

delay_seconds.description: Seconds to wait in the controller before this call starts. Prefer this over a `sleep` command: a shell sleep counts toward Worker call duration and misreports Worker performance.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds to allow the command to run before the Worker kills it, measured from execution start; the delay_seconds wait does not count. Defaults to 600.

worker.name: browser_control
worker.description: Control an isolated browser on the user's selected Worker. delay_seconds waits in the controller before the action starts.

delay_seconds.description: Seconds to wait in the controller before this call starts.

worker.name: computer_use
worker.description: Perform a user-device computer action through the selected Worker. delay_seconds waits in the controller before the action starts.

delay_seconds.description: Seconds to wait in the controller before this call starts.

normai_web_search.name: normai_web_search
normai_web_search.description: Search the web and return the result sources (title, URL, and snippet). Use it whenever the user asks about current events, recent releases, prices, or any fact that may have changed since your knowledge; run more searches when one query is not enough, and cite the sources in your reply.

query.description: The search query, written like a search engine query. Split complex questions into several targeted searches.

normai_image_generation.name: normai_image_generation
normai_image_generation.description: Generate an image from a text prompt and attach it to this conversation for the user to see. Use it whenever the user asks for a picture, illustration, diagram, or any other visual. Describe the subject, style, colors, and composition fully in the prompt. To edit or derive from pictures the user attached to their input, pass the one-based positions of those pictures in reference_images (for example [1] for the first attached picture, at most 4); without reference_images it creates a new image from the prompt alone.

prompt.description: Complete description of the image to generate.

reference_images.description: One-based positions of the pictures attached to the user's input to use as references, for example [1] for the first attached picture. Omit to create a new image from the prompt alone.
